system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding

- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall read:** the Seller package is a low-cap, broad-disclosure, everything-subject-to-limitations structure. Several of the "settled" items push real cash and risk items (Riverlark debt, closing bonuses, Ironquay IP, the DD-006 incident) onto the Company post-Completion, which cuts directly across the debt-free/cash-free baseline. Also note the Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026 — six weeks stale as of today — so any position below assumes a refreshed data room cut-off and a bring-down at signing and Completion.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- *Buyer wants:* General warranties ≥ 50% of price (fallback 30–35%); Fundamental/Title, Tax and specific indemnities at 100%; fraud uncapped.
- *Recommendation:* Counter at 50% general / 100% fundamental, tax and indemnities. **Reason:** 20% is light for a business with 30% revenue concentration, an open IP title gap and an unresolved privacy incident.

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket (excess only).
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 10k de minimis; AUD 250k *tipping* basket (first-dollar recovery once tipped); related/series claims aggregated; no thresholds for Fundamental/Title, Tax, specific indemnities or fraud.
- *Recommendation:* Tipping basket with aggregation of connected claims. **Reason:** the Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k) already show how a deductible basket plus per-claim de minimis can be structured around.

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; plus a default that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months general (captures a full audit cycle); Tax = 7 years / ATO amendment period + 90 days; Fundamental/Title = 7 years; specific indemnities = their own periods; the "applies to all Claims" default deleted.
- *Recommendation:* 24 months general and reject the catch-all default. **Reason:** the default clause is a drafting device to collapse every category into the weakest regime.

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap, thresholds and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime — 100% of price, no de minimis/basket, 7 years (or no limit), outside exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
- *Recommendation:* Reject outright. **Reason:** if title fails the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; recovering AUD 4.8m is not "administrative simplicity", it is an 80% haircut.

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* None. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- *Buyer wants:* Express carve-out for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and dishonesty from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
- *Recommendation:* Insert as a non-negotiable. **Reason:** a purported exclusion of liability for fraud is unlikely to be enforced anyway, but the absence of an express carve-out invites argument and is a market-standard omission a seller should not resist.

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- *Buyer wants:* "Fair disclosure" standard — only matters disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room disclosure; public searches limited to named registers (ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court lists) on a specified date; no new disclosure against the Completion warranties without a walk/price-adjust right.
- *Recommendation:* Reject general disclosure; require specific disclosure against each warranty. **Reason:** blanket disclosure of an unindexed data room, combined with cl 8.3, would effectively neutralise the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- *Buyer wants:* Delete. Fallback: only *actual* knowledge of two or three named deal-team individuals, limited to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, with no imputed, constructive or adviser knowledge.
- *Recommendation:* Delete; fallback as above. **Reason:** "discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test that converts every DD document into a disclosure, regardless of whether anyone read or understood it.

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of any written consent. No consent or evidence of satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit only (Buyer may waive): unconditional written consent in an agreed form, evidence cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, no change to commercial terms/pricing/term, and a Bluefen confirmation of no intention to terminate or renegotiate; Seller "best"/"all reasonable" endeavours; long-stop date; any consent conditioned on amended terms requires Buyer approval.
- *Recommendation:* Hard CP in agreed form. **Reason:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; a consent "satisfied on delivery" of whatever Bluefen chooses to send is not protection.

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "following Completion".
- *Buyer wants:* Payout letter obtained pre-Completion; facility repaid at Completion from the purchase price via the funds flow; deed of release and PPSR discharge (and any director guarantees released) delivered *at* Completion; cl 8.1 change-of-control addressed by payout, not consent.
- *Recommendation:* Make repayment and release a Completion deliverable funded by price deduction. **Reason:** the deal is debt-free/cash-free — a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company whose assets remain secured for AUD 3.2m with no contractual mechanism to force discharge.

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses (DD-005)**
- *Seller:* AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- *Buyer wants:* Treat as Transaction Expenses/Debt-like item deducted from the price, grossed up for superannuation (12%), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and other on-costs (roughly AUD 500k all-in); paid through the funds flow or by the Seller before Completion; specific uncapped indemnity for any shortfall; employee acknowledgements that no further amounts are owed.
- *Recommendation:* Price deduction of the grossed-up amount plus indemnity. **Reason:** bonuses triggered by Completion are Seller-caused leakage; if they sit in the Company unfunded, the Buyer pays them twice — once in price, once in cash.

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity (DD-004 / DD-010)**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010) and "considered adequate".
- *Buyer wants:* Pre-Completion payment of all SOW3 fees with bank evidence, plus a signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, as a CP/Completion deliverable; indemnity covering *all* loss from failure of SOW3 Project Materials to vest in the Company (third-party claims, licence fees, re-development, injunction/business interruption), separate 100% cap, no thresholds, 7-year period.
- *Recommendation:* CP + broad indemnity. **Reason:** the exposure is ownership of the IP under cl 7.3, not the AUD 180k invoice — an indemnity capped at the invoice covers the wrong risk.

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material; no breach admitted, no loss stated.
- *Buyer wants:* Completed investigation and documented NDB-scheme assessment (the 30-day assessment window has likely already run from 22 September) before signing, or as a CP; evidence of recall/deletion confirmation from the recipient; specific indemnity for all loss (OAIC/notification costs, remediation, third-party and customer claims, contractual penalties under Bluefen/Mossvale, civil penalties), uncapped or at 100%, no thresholds, 7 years; warranty on no other incidents.
- *Recommendation:* Specific indemnity plus completed assessment as a CP. **Reason:** ~1,240 records of identifiable individuals with unknown access status is an unquantified regulatory and customer-contract risk the Seller cannot simply label "not material".

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110k (AUD 330k) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- *Buyer wants:* Full terms of each renewal; confirmation of whether committed pre-Completion, terminable, and whether the benefit accrues post-Completion; if committed but unpaid at Completion, treated as debt-like/working-capital in the completion accounts; express aggregation as a single related matter for threshold purposes; specific indemnity if not terminable on standard notice.
- *Recommendation:* Aggregate and run through completion accounts or price. **Reason:** three identical AUD 110k items split across two DD documents, each below the basket and comfortably above the de minimis, looks structured — treat them as one.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- *Seller:* Single regime — all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated; exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- *Buyer wants:* Distinct categories with their own cap, thresholds, time limit and carve-outs: (1) General warranties; (2) Fundamental/Title; (3) Tax; (4) Specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, leakage); (5) Fraud. Clause 12 limitations apply only to category (1); a schedule sets out which limits apply to which category.
- *Recommendation:* Reject the unified regime and table a limitations matrix. **Reason:** without separation, the specific indemnities become worthless because they are swallowed by the 20% cap, AUD 250k basket and 18-month cut-off.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company's own share register at DD-012; expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent searches (ASIC current and historical extract, PPSR against the Seller and the Company — the Riverlark security should appear, constitution for pre-emptive rights, share certificates, any trust/nominee arrangements); full title warranties — Seller is sole legal and beneficial owner, shares fully paid, free of encumbrances, no options or convertible rights; Completion deliverables of executed transfers, certificates and register updates.
- *Recommendation:* Run the searches now and take uncapped title warranties. **Reason:** a share register is the Company's self-generated record, not independent evidence, and the Seller has pointedly told us it is not.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, thresholds).
- *Buyer wants:* Standalone tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax (100% cap, no thresholds, 7 years/amendment period + 90 days) and tax warranties; IP warranties on ownership, registration, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments, moral-rights consents, open-source compliance, with cap at 100% and ≥ 3–7 years; completion-date tax return / straddle-period mechanics.
- *Recommendation:* Reject and table separate tax and IP schedules. **Reason:** Ironquay already demonstrates an IP ownership gap in this business, and ATO exposures surface on audit well beyond 18 months.

---

**Other points to flag (not in the list, but relevant):**
- *DD-007 office lease* — obtain the notification wording; confirm whether notice converts into a landlord consent/termination right on change of control.
- *DD-009 Mossvale* — the assignment restriction may not bite on a share sale, but confirm there is no separate change-of-control or key-person clause.
- *Stale disclosure* — insist on a refreshed data-room cut-off and a schedule of changes since 22 September 2026 before the next turn of the SPA.

If helpful, I can convert this into a limitations matrix (category × cap × threshold × period × carve-outs) for the mark-up and a draft of the specific indemnity clauses for Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006.
=== END ADVICE ===
